replies.author: @beachhobbies
replies.text: @Singlesix6Correct, well written, thank you.  Here in Rodanthe we are a barrier island, the first one in NC, I like to think the outer banks stop at Oregon Inlet, everything north of the inlet is a peninsula of Virginia, call it an outer bank if you will.    Folks just like to say it for some reason.     Hatteras Island is not the outer banks.   Most folks do not realize that Nags Head through Carova is part of Virginia mainland

replies.author: @Singlesix6
replies.text:
@beachhobbies No it isn't. The term you are looking for is barrier islands.
The Outer Banks of NC are well defined. They end on the southern end at Ocracoke inlet. Across the inlet is Portsmouth Island with its preserved buildings from the abandoned Portsmouth Village. They begin the Core Banks.
"• North Core Banks: Stretches roughly 21 miles from Portsmouth Village to Ophelia Inlet.
• South Core Banks: Stretches roughly 21 miles down to Cape Lookout and Barden Inlet, featuring the Cape Lookout Lighthouse and wild Banker ponies."

replies.text: Nothing peaceful about this place. It used to be about 23 years ago, now it's just like what happened to Ocean City.  Heavy traffic - it can take hours to go 15 miles, rude tourists, some even ramming their carts at the grocery store. Every type of trash imaginable left at the beaches - some they bury, others like condoms they just throw on the ground. Loud at night, people partying, honking horns, screaming. Many of us can move out of the area and some have, but the wildlife are trapped - especially the wild horses, the news doesn't pick up on how many have been killed - hit by vehicles, I transported a horse that got shot.  The real truth gets buried because tourism seems to be the most important for politicians.
